decoded_pov.dedup: __asan_memmove--pcpp::RawPacket::insertData(int, unsigned char const*, unsigned long)--pcpp::Packet::extendLayer(pcpp::Layer*, int, unsigned long)

analyzed_vuln.description: `Packet::extendLayer()` does not validate that `offsetInLayer` is within `[0, layer->getDataLen()]` before computing `indexToInsertData = layer->m_Data + offsetInLayer - m_RawPacket->getRawData()` and calling `RawPacket::insertData()`. With an out-of-range/negative effective index, `RawPacket::insertData()` executes `memmove(..., m_RawDataLen - atIndex)` where `atIndex` is invalid, causing an underflow/negative size passed to memmove (ASan `negative-size-param`). Crash is observed in `RawPacket::insertData`, but root cause is missing bounds checks in `Packet::extendLayer` caller path.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In the fuzzer path (`FuzzTarget.cpp` -> `readParsedPacket`), malformed BGP UPDATE content leads `BgpUpdateMessageLayer::setNetworkLayerReachabilityInfo()` to call `extendLayer(...)` with an insertion offset derived from inconsistent parsed lengths (withdrawn routes/path attributes/NLRI layout). Because `extendLayer` trusts this offset and does not sanity-check it against layer boundaries/raw packet bounds, `insertData` performs memmove with invalid length (`m_RawDataLen - atIndex` becomes negative when interpreted by ASan), triggering the crash.
